content:
Facts: Deceased's cousins challenged 2017 holographic will appointing guardian sole heir claiming fraud/testamentary-capture by defendant who allegedly induced guardian-appointment and will-drafting; cited guardian's constant-contact, key-possession, asset-management, policy-beneficiary-change attempt; defendant contested claiming thirty-year friendship-relationship, asset-management continuation post-spouse-death, guardian-appointment avoiding general-power-attorney discretion, will reflecting deceased's family-estrangement intent.
Legal Framework: Articles 590, 624 Italian Civil Code (null-will validation; fraud/violence annulment); Art. 2697 Civil Code (burden of proof); case law on fraud requirements (Cass. 30424/2022, 8047/2001, 824/2014).
Interpretive Issues: Probative-requirements establishing testamentary-fraud/capture; whether support-administrator appointment evidences will-coercion; relevance of testator's education-level/age for fraud-assessment; burden-proof allocation for fraud-allegations; effect of long-standing relationship on capture-inference; admissibility of handwriting-expert/psychological-assessment requests when exploratory; standing-proof requirements for legitimate-succession heirs.
Principles Applied: Plaintiffs proved standing filing appropriate documentation with first Art. 183(6) brief; objection rejected. Testamentary-fraud/capture challenge requires careful fact-reconstruction with offered-evidence. Documentation shows no conditions making deceased impressionable/prone others-influence causing decision-weaknesses/emotional-awareness diminution predisposing influenced-susceptibility. Medical-documentation: 2013 hospital-admission for heart-disease without other-pathological evidence; 2017 physiatrist-report certifying mobility-difficulties stating "cognitively-intact overall"; 2018 hospital-admission records showing deceased signed personal-data consent without delegation/help. Deceased capable understanding/willing regarding own-interests management; requiring only mobility-difficulty assistance. Guardianship-Judge order (24.5.2017) confirms: deceased requested support-administrator appointment representing need for help because physical-condition prevents properly-managing daily-needs/independently-looking-after interests, expressing support/guidance/assistance need; widow, no-children, lives-alone with carer-help needing bank-visit/property-management help. Support-administrator appointed with mere-assistance powers limited twelve-months. Plaintiffs participated guardianship-proceedings limiting themselves contesting defendant-appointment without raising deceased-incapacity objections. Preliminary-motions rejected as partly-documentary partly-irrelevant; investigating-judge order confirmed. Fraud-establishing testamentary-disposition requires fraudulent-means evidence which considering testator-age/health/mental-state were misleading-capable giving-rise false-representations directing-will in otherwise-untaken direction; suitability assessed broad-criteria when testator suffering senile-diseases causing decision-weaknesses/emotional-awareness weakening, easily-predisposed influenced by carers/day-companions. Mere-psychological pressure through solicitation/cajoling insufficient; requires additional-elements presenting unlawful-conduct characteristics misleading settlor inducing different-decision versus spontaneous-will decision. Plaintiffs provided no disputed-facts evidence; influence although presumptive must base certain-facts allowing influence-identification/reconstruction plus consequent testator decision-process influence. Handwriting-expert request cannot compensate lacking-evidence requiring rigorous-provision; investigating-magistrate disregarded as purely-exploratory considering plaintiff-expert concluded will deceased-attributable. Other technical-advice requests (environmental/cultural/psychological circumstances regarding education/age/health/emotional-condition, medication-type ascertainment) generic/exploratory given medical-certificate. Psychological-coercion must relate will-pre-drafting events; no evidence beyond guardian-appointment fact already-considered. Undated/unsigned document (plaintiff doc.46) shows deceased no-intention leaving assets family-members, particularly cousins, naming individuals outside-family circle. Document drafted using terminology/methods similar contested-will (both indicating natural-person heirs' first/last names with birth-dates). Thirty-year defendant-deceased acquaintance (undisputed) developed trust-relationship continuing post-husband death-2016; deceased confirmed before Guardianship-Judge: surveyor helps-me does-everything, without-him wouldn't-know what-to-do; known-him years since-husband alive, much-trust; honest assists-everything helping with-wife even health-needs. Defendant long-managing deceased financial-interests supporting various daily-needs given mobility-difficulties; cousins neither-present nor-interested every-need including personal; deceased herself confirmed guardianship-proceedings. Deceased intended granting general-power-attorney facilitating tasks; defendant suggested support-administrator providing greater-action-soundness assurance facing Guardianship-Judge scrutiny. Observation rules-out alleged captation; general-power-attorney would allow greater financial-interests-management discretion whereas guardianship subjects administrator-actions to guardianship-judge control. Alternative-administrator appointment exclusively based plaintiff-claim regarding mismanagement in condominium-management; filed judgment intervening incidenter-tantum on defendant-conduct referring exclusively defendant-brought damages-action for derogatory-statements deemed reputation-damaging. Overall plaintiff-offered evidence unsuitable/insufficient concluding defendant coerced deceased for guardian-appointment for exclusive-financial gain. Same-arguments rule-out defendant coerced deceased-will for sole-heir designation.
